statute_citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 65912.155 et seq. (Chapter 4.1.5; § 65912.157 as amended by SB 722, Stats. 2026, ch. 100)
summary: Local governments may not impose a height limit under 75 ft, a maximum density under 120 dwelling units per acre, or standards precluding a 3.5 residential FAR within 1/4 mile of a Tier 1 transit-oriented development stop (heavy rail or very high frequency commuter rail in an urban transit county). 120 is units per acre, not a unit cap.
effective_date_note: Code section effective 2026-01-01; bill digest: provisions "would not apply to a local agency until July 1, 2026, except as specified, or within unincorporated areas of counties until the 7th regional housing needs allocation cycle"
eligible_counties_note: Statute applies to any "urban transit county" (county with more than 15 passenger rail stations), not a fixed list; the previous 9-county list is not in the statute and is unconfirmed
min_parking_note: SB 79 chaptered text contains no parking-minimum elimination; parking ratios come from Gov. Code 65915 density bonus law
affordability_note: 65912.157(i) offers alternatives (e.g. 7% extremely low, 10% very low income units); a single percentage is not statutory
statutory_exclusions_note: Chapter incorporates Gov. Code 65913.4 (very high fire hazard severity zone bar) when streamlining is sought; historic/sea-level-rise sites may be excluded from density rules up to 10% of eligible area; HPOZ/coastal-commission/floodway list in earlier record is not in SB 79 text

short_name: TX SB 840 (Multifamily/Mixed-Use in Commercial Zones, Tex. Loc. Gov't Code ch. 218)
summary: In a city over 150,000 in a county over 300,000, multifamily (3+ units) and mixed-use residential (65%+ residential) must be allowed where zoning allows office, commercial, retail, warehouse or mixed use, without rezoning or variance, administratively approved. City may not limit density below the greater of the highest residential density in the city or 36 units/acre, height below the greater of the highest commercial height or 45 ft, or require more than one parking space per unit. Conversion rules (ch. 218 subch. C) cover office/retail/warehouse buildings 5+ years old.
municipality_pop_note: "population greater than 150,000 that is wholly or partly located in a county with a population greater than 300,000"
allowed_zoning: classifications allowing office, commercial, retail, warehouse or mixed-use
statutory_exclusions_note: 218.101(c): zoning classifications allowing heavy industrial use; land within 1,000 ft of existing heavy industrial use; within 3,000 ft of an airport or military base; clear zone or accident potential zone

statute_citation: A.R.S. § 9-461.18 (accessory dwelling units); A.R.S. § 9-462.10 (commercial/office multifamily conversion, cities 150,000+)

The earlier "duplex/triplex/fourplex within 1 mile of the central business district" claim is not in the statute text found.
